name: equal_weight_eligible_universe
title: Equal-weight eligible universe
source: idea.md, 'Supporting diagnostics' and the decision log of 2026-10-05
reproducibility_note: the original script was recovered on 2026-10-14 from the 2026-10-05 research session transcript and is kept verbatim beside this file; re-run unchanged on 2026-10-14 against the same frozen inputs it reproduced every reported figure exactly; the only difference is its own faithfulness check against the sealed trades (largest per-trade gap 0.0016 bps against 0.0020 bps then, well inside its 0.5 bps assertion)
method: every stock with a valid 252-return volatility on the same rebalance days, same next-open fills, same data and costs, held equal weight; both books use this same model, so the pair is like for like with each other but not with the fixed-notional book
evidential_weight: supporting diagnostic only: not a gate, not a verdict rule and not decisive; the primary evidence against the selection edge is the matched random-entry comparison and the G3.2 out-of-sample failure
assumptions: same dataset, eligibility, calendar, rebalance sessions and next-open fills as the run
universe book: every stock with a valid 252-return volatility on the rebalance day, equal weight, no ranking
time-weighted monthly periods from one execution open to the next; the last period ends at the last close
turnover cost 12 bps per side for each name added or dropped, as a share of the book
compounded growth; CAGR over calendar years (365.25 days); volatility of monthly returns times sqrt(12)
both books use this one model, so the figures are like for like with each other and not with the run's fixed-notional book
